rows.description: A person from a close family culture sees friends abroad living alone, paying for care and rarely visiting elders, and finds it lonely. Yet those friends prize freedom that collectivist life can limit.

rows.description: A young adult combines independence with real duty, supporting family in agreed ways while keeping their own life. Interdependence works best when it is freely chosen and fairly shared.

rows.description: A teenager wants the same phone or shoes as peers and feels embarrassed by a modest family. Talking about needs, wants and choices builds resilience against status pressure.

rows.subtopic: Money attitudes, family finances, gifting, borrowing between relatives
rows.description: A young earner is asked by a cousin or uncle for money and feels obligation, awkwardness and fear of not being repaid. A clear amount, a clear time and no false promises protect both money and relationship.

rows.subtopic: Money attitudes, family finances, gifting, borrowing between relatives
rows.description: A young adult sees parents keep income, debts or property secret and feels shut out. Money silence can protect pride but also hides risks; gentle open talk is often a sign of trust.
